## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppādavāra* ("Section on Origination" or "Arising"), designated as Ya 9.2.1, is a canonical Abhidhamma text comprising the first subdivision of the process section (*pavattivāra*, Ya 9.2) of the ninth chapter of the *Yamaka* [Catalog; Ronkin 2005]. Across the chapters of the *Yamaka*, doctrinal categories are systematically examined in a processual framework divided into origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination-and-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Ronkin 2005]. Methodologically, an *uppādavāra* sets up paired questions and analytical elucidations across the three temporal dimensions (present, past, and future) and according to person, place (plane of existence), and person and place together, formulated in both positive and negative modes [Nyanatiloka 2007]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus shows that Ya 9.2.1 shares massive formulaic phrasing across the Pali Abhidhamma, with 13,440 matches across 48 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its primary internal structural counterparts are the companion sections of the same chapter, the *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 9.2.3, over 3,500 matches) and *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 9.2.2, over 3,400 matches), along with equivalent *uppādavāra* sections elsewhere in the *Yamaka*, particularly Ya 10.2.1, Ya 3.2.1, Ya 5.2.1, and Ya 6.2.1 [DharmaNexus]. It also shows extensive reuse with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* and the subcommentarial *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further identifies tentative cross-language alignments with Sanskrit texts including Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā* and Nāgārjuna's *Bodhyāpattideśanāvṛtti*, as well as the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā-lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records no curated historical parallels for this section [SuttaCentral].
